title: Bridged Incident Dossier and Closure Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
======
This page defines the "Bridged Incident Dossier" (a compact, standard incident artifact created during bridged/major incidents) and the playbook for moving from active response to closure. The dossier is a lightweight single-file story containing the timeline, evidence, impact calculation, customer-status artifacts, and closure criteria required for handoff to the post-incident review team and downstream stakeholders.

Why this exists
----------------
- Reduce friction during handoff from incident responders to postmortem authors.
- Standardize evidence collection so enterprise/regulatory audits have consistent artifacts.
- Provide templated customer- and exec-facing messages that can be quickly adapted.
- Make SLA credit calculations and remediation actions reproducible.

Scope
-----
Applies to:
- All production degradations or outages that open a bridged incident (severity P1/P0/P1-high).
- Multi-tenant incidents where customer impact or SLA credit may be required.
Excludes: simulated game-days, maintenance windows (unless unexpected regressions occur).

Owners and roles
----------------
- Incident Commander (IC): owns dossier creation and earliest artifact completeness.
- Evidence Scribe: collects logs, traces, and KV cache snapshots.
- Bridge Operator: owns the bridge, recording timestamps and participant list.
- Customer Liaison (CL): drafts customer-facing templates and posts status updates.
- Postmortem Lead: owns closure, root cause analysis, and action-tracking after the incident is stabilized.

Bridged Incident Dossier: minimum contents checklist
--------------------------------------------------
The dossier must contain the following sections (presented here as a checklist to be completed during the bridge):
- Incident metadata: incident id, service(s) affected (service slugs), IC, bridge link, start and end times (UTC), incident severity.
- Short summary (1–3 sentences): what happened, user-visible impact.
- Timeline (annotated): at least 10 timestamps or major events with actor and rationale.
- Evidence packet pointers: links to logs, traces (trace IDs), perf dashboards, flamegraphs, and representative request samples.
- Metrics snapshots: pre-incident baseline and peak-impact metrics (error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput).
- Customer impact matrix: list of affected tenants, estimated % of requests impacted, and any MV/paid customers flagged for escalation.
- Temporary mitigations executed: config changes, fallbacks, throttles, reroutes.
- Stability decisions: rollbacks, model fallback triggers, autoscale events.
- Status page artifacts: final customer message versions, status-page ids, and timestamps of publication.
- SLA and credit calculation worksheet: inputs and computed credit amount (if applicable).
- Post-incident next steps: owners and target dates for remediation.

Bridged incident flow (quick reference)
-------------------------------------
1) Bridge open and IC assignment (T0). IC posts bridge link and basic metadata to incident system.
2) Evidence Scribe attaches initial artifacts: timestamped metrics snapshot and 3 representative logs.
3) Customer Liaison drafts an initial "we are investigating" status and posts truncated status to the status page.
4) Containment & mitigation loop: apply mitigations (circuit breakers, model fallback) and measure impact.
5) If mitigation successful, mark Stabilized and start Dossier completion and scheduled handoff to Postmortem Lead.
6) If mitigation fails or incident escalates, maintain bridge until recovery and then proceed to dossier close.

Triage and containment runbook excerpt (for model-serving latency SLO regressions)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Detect: alert when p99 latency > 1.5x SLO for 10 minutes and error rate > 0.5%.
- Immediate steps (first 10 minutes):
  1. IC: confirm alert validity, note thresholds that fired in dossier.
  2. Scribe: capture a 5-minute window of perf metrics and top 10 traces: CLI:
     curl -s "https://dash.internal/services/metrics?service=runtime&from=-5m&to=now" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > metrics-5m.json
  3. Runtime lead: examine KV cache eviction graphs and hot-shard counts.
  4. Apply fast mitigation: switch routing policy to regional fallback with query cap-of-50% (temporary).
- If errors persist after 15 minutes: consider model quantization rollback (two-step):
  a) Re-route 10% of traffic to cold model variant for verification.
  b) If verified healthy, escalate to 50% over 10 minutes.

Evidence collection template (copy into dossier)
------------------------------------------------
Table: (paste into the dossier as rows)
- metric_snapshot_pre: /dash/snapshots/2026-03-12-09-00.json
- metric_snapshot_peak: /dash/snapshots/2026-03-12-09-12.json
- representative_trace_ids: [span-12345, span-12398, span-12411]
- log_archive_links: /logs/incidents/INC-2026-0041/2026-03-12-bridge.tar.gz
- kv_cache_state: /artifacts/kv/kv-state-2026-03-12.tar.gz
- config_changes: list of commands and Git commit SHAs (see example below)

Example commands to capture config and state
------------------------------------------
- Capture running config (k8s):
  kubectl -n redwood get deploy serving-runtime -o yaml > serving-deploy-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).yaml
- Snapshot Redis/KV metadata:
  redis-cli --rdb rdb-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).rdb
- Preserve active model weights/variant pointer:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/serving/current/variant.json ./variant-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json

Customer/status page messaging (templated)
----------------------------------------
Use these short, editable templates for status-page posts and CS notifications. Replace bracketed tokens.
- Initial public status (First 15 minutes):
  Title: "Degraded inference latency in [region] — investigating"
  Body: "We are investigating reports of increased latency for inference requests in [region]. Our engineers have opened an incident (ID: [INC-ID]) and are actively investigating. We will post updates every 15 minutes or when there is a material change."
- Stabilized public status:
  Title: "Service stabilized — continued monitoring"
  Body: "We mitigated the issue impacting inference latency in [region]. We are monitoring to ensure steady performance and will publish a technical postmortem within 72 hours."
- Customer follow-up (direct to affected tenants):
  Subject: "[INC-ID] — Summary and next steps for [tenant]"
  Body: "Hi [Tenant Name],
We observed [estimated %] of your requests were impacted between [Tstart] and [Tend]. The root cause was [brief cause]. We applied [mitigation]. Our remediation plan is: 1) [action 1], 2) [action 2]. Your assigned CSM is [CSM name]."

SLA credit quick method (example)
--------------------------------
When an outage qualifies for a credit under our SLA, calculate using the service-level definition and time window:
- Inputs (must be present in dossier): incident start, incident end, total customer requests in window, measured impact % for that customer.
- Example computation:
  - Customer total monthly billable requests: 120,000
  - Impact window: 2 hours = 2/720 of monthly window (approx).
  - Estimated impacted requests: 120,000 * (2/720) * 0.6 impact = 200 requests
  - Credit policy: credit = pro-rated fee for impacted requests (finance formula reference F-002).
Record the full worksheet in the dossier and attach finance approval link.

Closure criteria (must be satisfied before postmortem handoff)
-------------------------------------------------------------
- Incident is stabilized: p99 latency <= SLO for a sustained 30-minute window.
- Dossier completion: at least 80% of the checklist present and timestamped artifacts uploaded.
- Customer communications: public status updated and CS notifications sent for flagged tenants.
- Action owners assigned for remediation items with target dates.
- Finance notified if SLA credit may be required.

Post-incident retrospective & game-day integration
------------------------------------------------
Agenda (90 minutes):
1. Incident timeline readout (10 minutes, IC)
2. Evidence review (10 minutes, Scribe)
3. Root cause language (15 minutes, technical owners)
4. Actions and owners (15 minutes)
5. Lessons learned and playbook changes (20 minutes)
6. Optional game-day run (20 minutes) — attempt the top mitigation step in a synthetic environment if safe.

Runbook retirement and continuous improvement
--------------------------------------------
- Each bridged incident that results in a new remediation >3 person-days creates a task to update the runbooks the mitigation touched.
- Runbook change owner must submit a PR to the runbook repo within 7 days, with a short changelog entry describing the update.

Templates and artifacts (quick links)
-----------------------------------
- Executive one-pager template: attach as "exec-brief.md" in the dossier.
- Postmortem rubric and severity-to-action mapping: link "/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-rubric-2025"
- Dossier starter JSON (machine readable) for automation:
  { "incident_id": "[INC-ID]", "start_time": "[T0]", "severity": "P1", "owner": "[IC]" }

RACI (abridged)
---------------
- Responsible: IC, Evidence Scribe, Bridge Operator
- Accountable: SRE Lead
- Consulted: Runtime Engineering, Product (if config changes affect features)
- Informed: Customer Success, Legal (if regulatory / data exposure)

Examples and corner cases
------------------------
- Silent degradation detection: if anomaly detection flagged gradual p99 drift over 3 hours (no bridge opened), run the "silent incident" lightweight dossier and schedule a remediation game-day.
- Multi-region failover: if failover to secondary region was performed, attach traffic split charts and extra verification traces for the secondary region.

Appendix: common short commands and snippets for Scribes
------------------------------------------------------
- Capture top error traces (temporary):
  curl -s "https://traces.internal/api/search?service=runtime&minDuration=200&limit=20" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > top-traces.json
- Export SLO dashboard snapshot via CLI:
  slo-cli snapshot --service runtime --output slo-snapshot-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).png

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary contact for dossier process questions: Aisha Patel (pager: pagerduty)
- Escalation to SRE lead: Diego Morales

Notes
-----
This playbook favors rapid, repeatable evidence collection and small standardized message templates to reduce cognitive load on responders during high-stress bridged incidents. Keep the dossier concise — the goal is a single coherent artifact that supports postmortem recommendations, SLA computations, and customer trust restoration.
